html:
Sierra Leone is a country on the Atlantic coast of West Africa, between Guinea and Liberia. It began as a British settlement for freed slaves and is shown on the map from 1815 to the present.

In 1787 British abolitionists sent a first group of poor Black Londoners to found a "Province of Freedom" on the peninsula. In 1792 about a thousand Black Loyalists, former slaves who had fought for Britain in the American Revolution and been settled in Nova Scotia, arrived and founded Freetown. Maroons from Jamaica followed.

After Britain banned the slave trade in 1807, Sierra Leone became a crown colony in 1808 and the base of the navy squadron that stopped slave ships. Tens of thousands of Africans freed from those ships were landed there. The settlers and freed Africans mixed into the Krio people, with their own English-based language. Fourah Bay College, founded in 1827, trained teachers and clergy for much of West Africa; Samuel Ajayi Crowther was its first student.

Britain declared a protectorate over the interior in 1896, and a tax on houses set off the Hut Tax War of 1898.

Sierra Leone became independent in 1961. One-party rule and corruption followed, and from 1991 to 2002 a brutal civil war, in which the rebel Revolutionary United Front paid for its war with diamonds and maimed civilians. British troops helped end it in 2000. The country was struck again by the Ebola epidemic of 2014 to 2016.
sum: Sierra Leone is a country on the Atlantic coast of West Africa, between Guinea and Liberia. It began as a British settlement for freed slaves and is shown on the map from 1815 to the present.
